description: Evidence-graded synthesis of the 10 most effective strategies for long-term fat loss and weight-loss maintenance with maximal preservation of skeletal muscle / fat-free mass.

ranking_methodology.description: How candidates were identified, scored (criteria C1-C5 with weights) and ranked; number of candidates evaluated; per-strategy weighted scores for the final top 10.

top_10_strategies.description: Exactly 10 items, ranks 1 to 10, each rank used once, ordered by rank ascending.

evidence_grade.description: Overall certainty of evidence for the outcome that justifies this strategy's rank.

evidence_grade_rationale.description: Why this grade: study designs, number of studies and participants, follow-up length, consistency, risk of bias, indirectness. Label claims as [ESTABLISHED], [PRELIMINARY] or [HYPOTHESIS].

effect_size_summary.description: Pooled effect sizes with 95% CI, I2, k studies, n participants, follow-up; absolute values (e.g. kg lean mass preserved, kg less regain at 12/24 months). Write 'not reported' where no effect size exists. No p-value-only statements.

long_term_weight_loss_mechanism.description: Why it works for long-term fat loss / maintenance: adherence, satiety, energy density, NEAT compensation, adaptive thermogenesis, self-regulation. Separate demonstrated mechanisms from hypotheses.

muscle_preservation_mechanism.description: How it protects skeletal muscle: MPS stimulation, mechanical tension, anti-catabolic signalling, energy availability. Flag when support comes only from acute MPS or mechanistic studies.

quantitative_targets.description: One target per line, format: Parameter: low-high unit | basis (e.g. g/kg BW, g/kg FFM, % TDEE, % BW/week) | population | [CitationIDs].

progression_and_adjustment_rules.description: Decision rules, e.g. what to change if fat loss stalls, strength drops or lean mass declines; transition from deficit to maintenance.

monitoring_metrics.description: What to measure, how often and with which method, plus target values.

population_applicability.description: Which populations the numbers were derived from (overweight/obesity, lean resistance-trained, older adults) and limits of transferability.

counter_evidence_and_uncertainties.description: Strongest contradicting studies and objections, with citation IDs.

citation_ids.description: IDs that must exist in references[].id.

physiological_targets_summary.description: Numeric targets for the active fat-loss phase. Use null only when no defensible evidence exists and explain why in basis.

population_context.description: Which population these targets apply to and how they differ for overweight/obesity, lean resistance-trained and older adults.

weekly_weight_loss_percent_bw.description: Rate range compatible with optimal lean mass retention.

basis.description: Include how to handle obesity (actual vs reference/adjusted body weight).

resistance_training_minimum_dose.description: Minimum effective dose to preserve muscle in a deficit: sessions/week, hard sets per muscle group per week, intensity (%1RM or RIR), progression.

diet_break_or_refeed_protocol.description: Evidence-based protocol or explicit statement that evidence is insufficient.

notes_and_basis.description: Evidence basis for minimum fat intake and any other caveats for these targets.

synergy_matrix.description: At least 6 items linking behavioral adherence factors with physiological muscle-protection factors.

conflicting_findings.description: Both sides with designs, populations, sample sizes and effect sizes.

key_limitations.description: At least 8 methodological limitations of the evidence base, each with its practical consequence for interpreting the results.

considered_but_excluded.description: Evaluated candidate strategies not in the top 10. Format: Strategy - reason for exclusion - [CitationIDs].

references.description: Every ID cited anywhere in the output, and only those. Only sources actually retrieved during this research.

id.description: FirstAuthorYear, letter suffix for duplicates, e.g. Helms2014a.

citation.description: Authors (first three, et al.), year, title, journal, volume(issue), pages.

design_population_n.description: Design details, population, sample size (or k studies / n participants), duration and follow-up.

url.description: https://doi.org/<DOI> preferred; otherwise https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/<PMID>/ or PMC URL.
